Disable the rexec service

findings.description:

findings.impact:
Attackers can exploit
                        this issue to execute arbitrary commands in the

findings.mitigation:
A whole cleanup of the infected

findings.title: Possible Backdoor: Ingreslock

findings.description:
Systems using Distributed Ruby (dRuby/DRb), which is available in
                        Ruby versions 1.6
                        and later, may permit unauthorized systems to execute distributed
                        commands.
findings.impact:
By default, Distributed Ruby does not
                        impose restrictions on allowed hosts or set the
                        $SAFE environment variable to prevent privileged activities. If other
                        controls are not in place, especially if the
                        Distributed Ruby process runs with elevated privileges, an attacker could
                        execute arbitrary system commands or Ruby
                        scripts on the Distributed Ruby server. An attacker may need to know only
                        the URI of the listening Distributed Ruby
                        server to submit Ruby commands.
findings.mitigation:
Administrators of
                        environments that rely on Distributed Ruby should ensure that
                        appropriate controls are in place. Code-level controls may include:

                        - Implementing taint on untrusted input

                        - Setting $SAFE levels appropriately (>2 is recommended if untrusted hosts
                        are allowed to submit Ruby commands, and >3 may be appropriate)

                        - Including drb/acl.rb to set ACLEntry to restrict access to trusted
                        hosts
findings.title: Distributed Ruby (dRuby/DRb) Multiple Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities

findings.description:
The Operating System (OS) on the remote host has reached the End
                        of Life (EOL) and should not be used
                        anymore.
findings.impact:
An EOL version of an OS is not
                        receiving any security updates
                        from the vendor. Unfixed security vulnerabilities might be leveraged by an
                        attacker to compromise
                        the security of this host.
findings.mitigation:
Upgrade the OS on the
                        remote host to a version which is still
                        supported and receiving security updates by the
                        vendor.
findings.title: Operating System (OS) End of Life (EOL) Detection

findings.description:
TWiki is prone to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and Command Execution
                        Vulnerabilities.
findings.impact:
Successful exploitation could allow
                        execution of arbitrary script code or
                        commands. This could let attackers steal cookie-based authentication
                        credentials or compromise the affected
                        application.
findings.mitigation:
Upgrade to version 4.2.4 or
                        later.
findings.title: TWiki XSS and Command Execution Vulnerabilities

findings.description:
DistCC is prone to a remote code execution (RCE)
                        vulnerability.
findings.impact:
DistCC by default trusts its
                        clients completely that in turn
                        could allow a malicious client to execute arbitrary commands on the
                        server.
findings.mitigation:
Vendor updates are available. Please see
                        the references for
                        more information.

                        For more information about DistCC's security see the
                        references.
findings.title: DistCC RCE Vulnerability (CVE-2004-2687)

findings.description: Try to log in with given passwords via VNC protocol.
findings.mitigation:
Change the password to something hard
                        to guess or enable
                        password protection at all.
findings.title: VNC Brute Force Login

findings.description:
It was possible to login into the remote PostgreSQL as user
                        postgres using weak credentials.
findings.mitigation:
Change
                        the password as soon as possible.
findings.title: PostgreSQL Default Credentials (PostgreSQL Protocol)

findings.description:
UnrealIRCd is prone to authentication spoofing
                        vulnerability.
findings.impact:
Successful exploitation
                        of this vulnerability
                        will allows remote attackers to spoof certificate fingerprints and
                        consequently
                        log in as another user.
findings.mitigation:
Upgrade to UnrealIRCd 3.2.10.7,
                        or 4.0.6, or later.
findings.title: UnrealIRCd Authentication Spoofing Vulnerability

findings.description:
It was possible to login into the remote FTP server using
                        weak/known credentials.
findings.impact:
This issue may be exploited by a
                        remote attacker to e.g. gain
                        access to sensitive information or modify system configuration.
findings.mitigation:
Change the password as soon as
                        possible.
findings.title: FTP Brute Force Logins Reporting

findings.description:
Misconfigured web servers allows remote clients to perform
                        dangerous HTTP methods such as PUT and
                        DELETE.
findings.impact:
- Enabled PUT
                        method: This might allow an attacker to upload
                        and run arbitrary code on this web server.

                        - Enabled DELETE method: This might allow an attacker to delete additional
                        files on this web
                        server.
findings.mitigation:
Use access restrictions to
                        these dangerous HTTP methods
                        or disable them completely.
findings.title: Test HTTP dangerous methods

findings.description:
vsftpd is prone to a backdoor
                        vulnerability.
findings.impact:
Attackers can exploit this issue
                        to execute arbitrary commands in the
                        context of the application. Successful attacks will compromise the affected
                        application.
findings.mitigation:
The repaired package can
                        be downloaded from
                        the referenced link. Please validate the package with its
                        signature.
findings.title: vsftpd Compromised Source Packages Backdoor Vulnerability

findings.description:
Many PHP installation tutorials instruct the user to create
                        a file called phpinfo.php or similar containing the phpinfo() statement.
                        Such a file is often
                        left back in the webserver
                        directory.
findings.impact:
Some of the
                        information that can be gathered from this file includes:

                        The username of the user running the PHP process, if it is a sudo user, the
                        IP address of the host, the web server
                        version, the system version (Unix, Linux, Windows, ...), and the root
                        directory of the web server.
findings.mitigation:
Delete the listed files
                        or restrict access to them.
findings.title: phpinfo() output Reporting

findings.description:
PHP is prone to an information-disclosure
                        vulnerability.
findings.impact:
Exploiting this issue allows remote
                        attackers to view the source code of files in the
                        context of the server process. This may allow the attacker to obtain
                        sensitive information and to run arbitrary PHP code
                        on the affected computer. Other attacks are also possible.
findings.mitigation:
PHP has
                        released version 5.4.3 and 5.3.13 to address this vulnerability.
                        PHP is recommending that users upgrade to the latest version of
                        PHP.
findings.title: PHP-CGI-based setups vulnerability when parsing query string parameters from php files.

findings.description:
The remote Riello NetMan 204 network card is using known default
                        credentials for the SSH login.
findings.impact:
This
                        issue may be exploited by a remote attacker to gain access
                        to sensitive information or modify system configuration.
findings.mitigation:
Change the
                        password of the affected account(s).
findings.title: Riello NetMan 204 Default Credentials (SSH)

findings.description: OpenSSL is prone to security-bypass vulnerability.
findings.impact:
Successfully exploiting this
                        issue may allow attackers to obtain
                        sensitive information by conducting a man-in-the-middle attack. This may
                        lead to other attacks.
findings.mitigation:
Updates are available.
                        Please see the references for more
                        information.
findings.title: SSL/TLS: OpenSSL CCS Man in the Middle Security Bypass Vulnerability

findings.description:
TWiki is prone to a cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
                        vulnerability.
findings.impact:
Successful exploitation will allow
                        attacker to gain administrative
                        privileges on the target application and can cause CSRF
                        attack.
findings.mitigation:
Upgrade to TWiki version 4.3.2 or
                        later.
findings.title: TWiki Cross-Site Request Forgery Vulnerability - Sep10

findings.description:
Reports if the remote FTP Server allows anonymous
                        logins.

Based on the files accessible via
                        this anonymous FTP login and
                        the permissions of this account an attacker might be able to:

                        - gain access to sensitive files

                        - upload or delete files.
findings.mitigation:
If you do
                        not want to share files, you should disable anonymous
                        logins.
findings.title: Anonymous FTP Login Reporting

Update to version 1.9.0 or
                        later.
findings.title: jQuery < 1.9.0 XSS Vulnerability

bin/statistics in TWiki 6.0.2 allows XSS via the webs

findings.description:
Samba is prone to a vulnerability that allows attackers to
                        execute arbitrary shell commands because the software fails to sanitize
                        user-supplied input.
findings.impact:
An attacker may leverage this issue
                        to execute arbitrary shell
                        commands on an affected system with the privileges of the
                        application.
findings.mitigation:
Updates are
                        available. Please see the referenced vendor
                        advisory.
findings.title: Samba MS-RPC Remote Shell Command Execution Vulnerability - Active Check

findings.description:
It was possible to detect the usage of the deprecated SSLv2
                        and/or SSLv3 protocol on this system.
findings.impact:
An attacker might be able
                        to use the known cryptographic flaws to
                        eavesdrop the connection between clients and the service to get access to
                        sensitive data
                        transferred within the secured connection.

                        Furthermore newly uncovered vulnerabilities in this protocols won't receive
                        security updates
                        anymore.
findings.mitigation:
It is recommended to disable the
                        deprecated SSLv2 and/or SSLv3
                        protocols in favor of the TLSv1.2+ protocols. Please see the references for
                        more information.
findings.title: SSL/TLS: Deprecated SSLv2 and SSLv3 Protocol Detection

findings.description:
The remote web server supports the TRACE and/or TRACK
                        methods. TRACE and TRACK are HTTP methods which are used to debug web server
                        connections.
findings.impact:
An attacker may use this flaw
                        to trick your legitimate web
                        users to give him their credentials.
findings.mitigation:
Disable the TRACE and TRACK methods in
                        your web server
                        configuration.

                        Please see the manual of your web server or the references for more
                        information.
findings.title: HTTP Debugging Methods (TRACE/TRACK) Enabled

findings.description:
The remote SSH server is configured to allow / support weak key
                        exchange (KEX) algorithm(s).
findings.impact:
An attacker can quickly break
                        individual connections.
findings.mitigation:
Disable the reported weak KEX
                        algorithm(s)

                        - 1024-bit MODP group / prime KEX algorithms:

                        Alternatively use elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellmann in general, e.g. Curve
                        25519.
findings.title: Weak Key Exchange (KEX) Algorithm(s) Supported (SSH)

findings.description:
The remote SSH server is configured to allow / support weak host
                        key algorithm(s).
findings.mitigation:
Disable the
                        reported weak host key
                        algorithm(s).
findings.title: Weak Host Key Algorithm(s) (SSH)

findings.description:
This routine reports all Weak SSL/TLS cipher suites accepted
                        by a service.

                        NOTE: No severity for SMTP services with 'Opportunistic TLS' and weak cipher
                        suites on port
                        25/tcp is reported. If too strong cipher suites are configured for this
                        service the alternative
                        would be to fall back to an even more insecure cleartext
                        communication.
findings.mitigation:
The
                        configuration of this services should be changed so
                        that it does not accept the listed weak cipher suites anymore.

                        Please see the references for more resources supporting you with this
                        task.
findings.title: SSL/TLS: Report Weak Cipher Suites

findings.description:
The /doc directory is browsable.
                        /doc shows the content of the /usr/doc directory and therefore it shows
                        which programs and - important! - the version of the installed
                        programs.
findings.mitigation:
Use access restrictions
                        for the /doc directory.
                        If you use Apache you might use this in your access.conf:

                        <Directory /usr/doc>
                        AllowOverride None
                        order deny, allow
                        deny from all
                        allow from localhost
                        </Directory>
findings.title: /doc directory browsable

findings.description:
The remote server's SSL/TLS certificate has already
                        expired.
findings.mitigation:
Replace the SSL/TLS certificate by a
                        new one.
findings.title: SSL/TLS: Certificate Expired

findings.description:
awiki is prone to multiple local file include (LFI)
                        vulnerabilities because it fails to properly sanitize user-supplied
                        input.
findings.impact:
An attacker can exploit this
                        vulnerability to obtain potentially
                        sensitive information and execute arbitrary local scripts in the context of
                        the webserver
                        process. This may allow the attacker to compromise the application and the
                        host.
findings.mitigation:
No known solution was made
                        available for at least one year
                        since the disclosure of this vulnerability. Likely none will be provided
                        anymore. General
                        solution options are to upgrade to a newer release, disable respective
                        features, remove the
                        product or replace the product by another
                        one.
findings.title: awiki <= 20100125 Multiple LFI Vulnerabilities - Active Check

findings.description:
The host / application transmits sensitive information (username,
                        passwords) in
                        cleartext via HTTP.
findings.impact:
An attacker could use this
                        situation to compromise or eavesdrop on the
                        HTTP communication between the client and the server using a
                        man-in-the-middle attack to get access to
                        sensitive data like usernames or passwords.
findings.mitigation:
Enforce the
                        transmission of sensitive data via an encrypted SSL/TLS connection.
                        Additionally make sure the host / application is redirecting all users to
                        the secured SSL/TLS connection before
                        allowing to input sensitive data into the mentioned
                        functions.
findings.title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information via HTTP

findings.description:
The remote host is running a VNC server providing one or more
                        insecure or
                        cryptographically weak Security Type(s) not intended for use on untrusted
                        networks.
findings.impact:
An attacker can uncover
                        sensitive data by sniffing traffic to the
                        VNC server.
findings.mitigation:
Run the session over an
                        encrypted channel provided by IPsec [RFC4301] or SSH [RFC4254].
                        Some VNC server vendors are also providing more secure Security Types within
                        their products.
findings.title: VNC Server Unencrypted Data Transmission

findings.description:
The remote host is running a FTP service that allows cleartext
                        logins over
                        unencrypted connections.
findings.impact:
An attacker can uncover login
                        names and passwords by sniffing traffic to the
                        FTP service.
findings.mitigation:
Enable
                        FTPS or enforce the connection via the 'AUTH TLS' command. Please see
                        the manual of the FTP service for more
                        information.
findings.title: FTP Unencrypted Cleartext Login

findings.description:
It was possible to detect the usage of the deprecated TLSv1.0
                        and/or TLSv1.1 protocol on this system.
findings.impact:
An attacker might be able to
                        use the known cryptographic flaws
                        to eavesdrop the connection between clients and the service to get access to
                        sensitive data
                        transferred within the secured connection.

                        Furthermore newly uncovered vulnerabilities in this protocols won't receive
                        security updates
                        anymore.
findings.mitigation:
It is recommended to disable
                        the deprecated TLSv1.0 and/or
                        TLSv1.1 protocols in favor of the TLSv1.2+ protocols. Please see the
                        references for more
                        information.
findings.title: SSL/TLS: Deprecated TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 Protocol Detection

findings.description:
phpMyAdmin is prone to a cross-site scripting (XSS)
                        vulnerability.
findings.impact:
Successful
                        exploitation will allow attackers to inject arbitrary
                        HTML code within the error page and conduct phishing
                        attacks.
findings.mitigation:
No known solution
                        was made available for at least one year since the disclosure
                        of this vulnerability. Likely none will be provided anymore. General
                        solution options are to upgrade to a newer
                        release, disable respective features, remove the product or replace the
                        product by another one.
findings.title: phpMyAdmin 'error.php' Cross Site Scripting Vulnerability

findings.description:
jQuery is prone to a cross-site scripting (XSS)
                        vulnerability.
findings.mitigation:
Update to
                        version 1.6.3 or later.
findings.title: jQuery < 1.6.3 XSS Vulnerability

findings.description:
The remote SSH server is configured to allow / support weak
                        encryption algorithm(s).
findings.mitigation:
Disable the reported weak
                        encryption algorithm(s).
findings.title: Weak Encryption Algorithm(s) Supported (SSH)

findings.description:
TWiki is prone to a cross-site scripting (XSS)
                        vulnerability.
findings.impact:
Successful exploitation will allow
                        remote attackers to insert
                        arbitrary HTML and script code, which will be executed in a user's browser
                        session in the context of an affected site.
findings.mitigation:
No known solution was
                        made available for at least one year
                        since the disclosure of this vulnerability. Likely none will be provided
                        anymore. General solution
                        options are to upgrade to a newer release, disable respective features,
                        remove the product or
                        replace the product by another
                        one.
findings.title: TWiki 'organization' Cross-Site Scripting Vulnerability

findings.description:
The SSL/TLS service uses Diffie-Hellman groups with insufficient
                        strength
                        (key size < 2048).
findings.impact:
An attacker might be able to decrypt
                        the SSL/TLS communication offline.
findings.mitigation:
Deploy
                        (Ephemeral) Elliptic-Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE) or use
                        a 2048-bit or stronger Diffie-Hellman group (see the references).

                        For Apache Web Servers:
                        Beginning with version 2.4.7, mod_ssl will use DH parameters which include
                        primes with lengths of more than 1024
                        bits.
findings.title: SSL/TLS: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange Insufficient DH Group Strength Vulnerability

findings.description:
The remote service is using a SSL/TLS certificate in the
                        certificate chain that has been signed using a
                        cryptographically weak hashing algorithm.
findings.mitigation:
Servers that use
                        SSL/TLS certificates signed with a weak SHA-1, MD5, MD4 or MD2 hashing
                        algorithm will need to obtain new
                        SHA-2 signed SSL/TLS certificates to avoid web browser SSL/TLS certificate
                        warnings.
findings.title: SSL/TLS: Certificate Signed Using A Weak Signature Algorithm
